# Plan your visit

Welcome to Leighton House and Sambourne House!  Find here useful information to help plan your visit, from opening hours to admission prices and how to get to us.

### Visitor Feedback: Have your say!

Please help us improve our services by filling up our short feedback survey after your visit to Leighton House and Sambourne House:

[Museums visitor feedback](https://consult.rbkc.gov.uk/communities/e746e603)

## Visitor notice: Leighton House closed on 13 (from 4pm), 14 and 15 November

Due to a private event, Leighton House will be closed from 4pm on Friday 13 November (last entry 3:15pm) and all day on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November (10am - 5:30pm). The museum will reopen on Monday 16 November. Sambourne House will remain open as usual.

We apologise for any inconvenience. For related enquiries, please contact us on museums@rbkc.gov.uk

## Christmas opening times

Monday 21 December: Leighton House open; Sambourne House closed (standard closure).

Tuesday 22 December to Saturday 26 December: Leighton House and Sambourne House closed.

Sunday 27 December: Leighton House and Sambourne House open.

Monday 28 December: Leighton House open; Sambourne House closed (standard closure).

Tuesday 29 December: Leighton House and Sambourne House closed (standard closure).

Wednesday 30 December: Leighton House and Sambourne House open.

Thursday 31 December and Friday 1 January: Leighton House and Sambourne House closed.

## Opening times and last entry

Last entry to Leighton House and Sambourne House is 4.30pm. We reserve the right to refuse admission after this time.

If you have a joint ticket, allow enough time to enjoy both museums fully. The houses are an 8-minute walk apart.

The [De Morgan Café](https://www.rbkc.gov.uk/museums/de-morgan-cafe-leighton-house) at Leighton House opens 10am – 5pm, with last orders at 4:30pm. The café is closed on Tuesdays.

## How to get here

#### Underground

The following trains stations are located within 10-15 minute walk from Leighton House and Sambourne House.

High Street Kensington (District and Circle lines); Holland Park (Central line); Kensington Olympia (London Overground)

We recommend checking the [Transport for London](http://journeyplanner.tfl.gov.uk/user/XSLT_TRIP_REQUEST2?language=en&execInst=&sessionID=0&ptOptionsActive=-1&place_destination=London&name_destination=Leighton%20House%20Museum&type_destination=poi 'Transport for London') website prior to your journey to make sure there are no disruptions to your travel plans.

#### Buses

Routes 9, 23, 27, 28, 49, 328, C1 stop on Design Museum / Kensington High Street/ Earls Court Road. 

#### Cycling

There are two cycle racks at Leighton House, outside the main entrance. Unfortunately, there are no dedicated racks at Sambourne House, but there are nearby along Kensington High Street. 

#### Parking

There is no onsite parking or drop-off parking at either museums. We recommend travelling by public transport where possible.

For more parking information, see our [guide to parking](https://www.rbkc.gov.uk/parking-transport-and-streets/visitor-parking-and-pay-phone/guide-parking).

Front entrance at Leighton House

## Admission charges

An admission ticket offers you access to the historic interiors at Leighton House and Sambourne House. Temporary exhibitions at Leighton House are included with admission. Joint tickets offer admission to both museums.

You can buy tickets at Welcome Desk on the day or pre-book online in advance. Please note that online same-day tickets are note available. 

[**Buy tickets**](https://leightonhouse.digitickets.co.uk/tickets)

### Leighton House

- Adults: £14
- Concessions\*: £10
- Children (6 to 18 years): £6
- National Art Pass (Art Fund): 50% off entry. Valid proof required on arrival.
- RBKC employees\*\*: £7 _(at the door online, online booking is not available)_

### Sambourne House

- Adults: £12
- Concessions\*: £10
- Children (6 to 18 years): £6
- National Art Pass (Art Fund): 50% off entry. Valid proof required on arrival.
- RBKC employees\*\*: £7 _(at the door online, online booking is not available)_

### Joint tickets for both museums

- Adults: £23
- Concessions\*: £16
- Children (6 to18 years): £8
- National Art Pass (Art Fund): 50% off entry. Valid proof required on arrival.

**Concessions:**

Valid proof for concessionary rates will be required on arrival. Concessions apply to:

- Visitors aged 18 to 25 years old
- Full-time students (all ages)
- Visitors with disabilities
- Job seekers

### Free entry

- Children aged 6 years and under
- Accompanying carers
- Blue Badge Guides
- Members of The Friends
- Accredited press\*
- ICOM and Museums Association

_Accredited press can request a complimentary pass in advance by emailing Marketing Manager, Ana Garcia at_ ana.garcia@rbkc.gov.uk_._

#### Free to visit areas at Leighton House:

- Gift shop
- De Morgan Café
- Garden
- [Tavolozza Drawings Gallery](https://www.rbkc.gov.uk/museums/free-visit-areas-leighton-house)
- Art displays

#### Pay What You Want

Pay What you Want when you visit Leighton House on the first Monday of each month from 10am to 1pm. This means you can pay above the standard ticket price, the same or nothing at all. 

Tickets are only available at the door. Advance online booking on PWYW days is not available.

This offer is not available for group bookings or Bank Holidays.

#### Free volunteer-led tours

Our wonderful team of volunteers offer free guided tours with collections and interiors highlights. The free tours are included within an admission ticket and places are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis - if you are interested, please enquire about them at Welcome Desk on arrival. Unfortunately, since these tours depend on volunteer availability, they can't be guaranteed every week.

**Leighton House**: Wednesday and Sunday, 2.30pm to 3.15pm

**Sambourne House**: Wednesday and Saturday, 3pm to 3.45pm

Visitors at Sambourne House.

## Admission information

[View / Download Leighton House Map Floorplan](https://issuu.com/leighton-house_sambourne-house/docs/leighton_house_map_floorplan)

#### Bag size policy

All suitcases and bags larger than 55cm x 40cm x 20cm are not permitted at either museums. 

We do not recommend taking large backpacks into the historical areas of either Leighton House or Sambourne House.

#### Photography

The historic interiors at Leighton House and Sambourne House are highly photogenic so visitors are encouraged to photograph their favourite corners, objects and artworks (just avoid flash photography). If you would like to share on social media, please do tag @leightonsambournemuseums when possible!

Only hand-held cameras and phones are allowed. Tripods, monopods, gimbals and lighting are not permitted in the rooms.

Photography taken at the museums should remain for personal use. For For commercial photo shoots, contact our [Venue Hire](https://www.rbkc.gov.uk/museums/node/47) team.  

#### Pets

We welcome guide, hearing and service dogs to our museums. We are unable to welcome any other pets inside the historic houses and outdoor spaces (including the De Morgan Café at Leighton House) due to the Grade II listing of the building and the fragility of our collections.

## Facilities

### Leighton House

- There is a gift shop in the reception area, selling a curated selection of products inspired by our collections - you can also browse our [online shop](https://museumshop.rbkc.gov.uk).
- For light refreshments, visit the [De Morgan Café](https://www.rbkc.gov.uk/museums/de-morgan-cafe-leighton-house) on the ground floor, with access to the garden.
- The garden is open in good weather.
- There's no dedicated cloakroom at Leighton House. Suitcases and large bags are not permitted at either of our museums. This also helps preserve the delicate fabric of the historic interiors.
- Gender-neutral and accessible toilets including baby change facilities can be found on the lower ground floor.
- Benches, seating and portable folding stools are available across the historic rooms.

### Sambourne House

- There is a small gift shop in the the reception area.
- There is no café.
- There are a limited number of secure lockable racks for you to store some personal items during your visit however there is very limited space and no dedicated cloakroom on site. Suitcases and large bags are not permitted.
- Two gender-neutral toilets are found on the lower basement level without step-free access. Unfortunately, due to the historic nature of this museum, there are currently no accessible toilets or baby change facilities.
- There are a small number of portable folding stools across the historic interiors.

Shop and reception area at Leighton House

#### Lifts and step-free access

There are platform and passenger lifts at Leighton House which provide step free access to all floors of the museum. 

Unfortunately, there is not step-free access at Sambourne House.

#### Buggy access and parking

**At Leighton House,** buggies and push chairs can be used on all floors of the new wing and in the Learning Centre on the lower ground floor. Unfortunately, buggies and pushchairs can’t be taken into the historic house.

**At Sambourne House**, due to this historic nature of the museum, there is no access for buggies and pushchairs. A limited number of buggies can be parked in the lower basement level during your visit but please note that there is no step free access to the museum so any buggy or pushchair must be carried down a short, steep flight of steps to reach the basement reception.

## Accessibility

There is step free access to all floors of Leighton House.

There is no step free access to Sambourne House.

Find out more about our [Accessibility](https://www.rbkc.gov.uk/museums/accessibility). If you have any access enquiries contact museums@rbkc.gov.uk ahead of your visit so we can provide you with appropriate assistance.
